vuln.description: vsftpd 2.3.4 contains a backdoor triggered by a smiley face in the username field (USER :)) which opens a shell on port 6200. Additionally, anonymous FTP login is allowed, exposing file system contents.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected vsftpd 2.3.4 running on port 21/tcp with anonymous FTP enabled (FTP code 230)
vuln.remediation: Upgrade to vsftpd 2.3.5 or later. Remove the compromised binary. Disable anonymous FTP access.

vuln.description: OpenSSH 4.7p1 uses weak cryptographic algorithms including deprecated DSA keys (1024-bit) and may support weak ciphers. This version is end-of-life and lacks modern security features.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected OpenSSH 4.7p1 on port 22/tcp with 1024-bit DSA host key
vuln.remediation: Upgrade to OpenSSH 8.0 or later. Disable weak ciphers and key exchange algorithms. Replace DSA keys with Ed25519 or RSA 4096-bit keys.

vuln.description: Telnet transmits all data including usernames and passwords in cleartext over the network. Any network sniffer can capture credentials and session data.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected Linux telnetd running on port 23/tcp
vuln.remediation: Disable telnet service immediately. Use SSH for remote access instead. Block port 23 at the firewall level.

vuln.description: SMTP service supports deprecated SSLv2 protocol with weak export-grade ciphers (40-bit RC4/RC2). SSLv2 is vulnerable to DROWN attacks and cipher downgrade. Certificate expired in 2010.
vuln.evidence: nmap script detected SSLv2 enabled on port 25/tcp with weak ciphers including SSL2_RC4_128_EXPORT40_WITH_MD5. SSL certificate expired 2010-04-16.
vuln.remediation: Disable SSLv2 and SSLv3. Configure TLS 1.2 or higher only. Use strong cipher suites. Renew SSL certificate.

vuln.category: End-of-Life Software — DNS Cache Poisoning Risk
vuln.description: ISC BIND 9.4.2 is severely outdated (released 2007) and end-of-life. Multiple critical vulnerabilities exist in this version including cache poisoning, denial of service, and potential remote code execution flaws discovered over the years.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected ISC BIND 9.4.2 on port 53/tcp via dns-nsid script
vuln.remediation: Upgrade to ISC BIND 9.18 or later. Consider using a maintained DNS server like PowerDNS or Unbound.

vuln.category: Denial of Service — Range Header Attack
vuln.description: Apache 2.2.8 is vulnerable to the ByteRange DoS attack where specially crafted Range headers cause memory exhaustion. Server also exposes phpinfo revealing detailed configuration. WebDAV is enabled increasing attack surface.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected Apache httpd 2.2.8 on port 80/tcp. Gobuster found /phpinfo.php (48KB) and /dav directory. X-Powered-By header reveals PHP/5.2.4-2ubuntu5.10.
vuln.remediation: Upgrade to Apache 2.4.x. Remove phpinfo.php. Disable WebDAV if not required. Update PHP to supported version.

vuln.description: RPC service exposes detailed information about running services including NFS (ports 2049), mountd, nlockmgr, and status. This information aids attackers in service enumeration and planning targeted attacks.
vuln.evidence: nmap rpcinfo script enumerated 10 RPC services including NFS v2/3/4 on ports 2049 TCP/UDP
vuln.remediation: Restrict rpcbind to localhost only if not required for legitimate clients. Use firewall rules to block external access to port 111 and related RPC services.

vuln.category: Remote Code Execution — Username Map Script
vuln.description: Samba 3.0.20 allows attackers to execute arbitrary commands by sending shell metacharacters in the username during authentication. SMB message signing is disabled, allowing man-in-the-middle attacks. Guest authentication is enabled.
vuln.evidence: nmap detected Samba 3.0.20-Debian on ports 139 and 445. SMB security scan shows guest account enabled, message signing disabled, system time reveals hostname metasploitable.localdomain.
vuln.remediation: Upgrade Samba to >= 3.0.25 or current stable (4.x). Disable username map script. Enable SMB signing. Disable guest access.
